approval.note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI draft 2021 (gastric cancer): needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI draft 2021, gastric cancer (page 1: flow chart with work-up and settings; page 2: PET, CDH1 testing, endoscopy, EUS): needs a clinician's check. The file prints no tier letters, so every tier is a proposal (an item in the page 1 work-up block is proposed Essential; 'desirable' and 'encouraged' are proposed Optimal; 'consider' is proposed Optional), to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). PET: page 2 says 'PET scan should NOT be performed in gastric cancer', so no PET record is listed. MMR / MSI is not in this file and is not listed. The system records the stage as written and never computes it; no treatment advice. India first: the National Cancer Grid draft is the only source (page 1 uses 'Poor PS/ ASA 4'; page 2 says EMR and follow up belong at tertiary care centres).
settings_note: The setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes a stage and never decides the setting). Each record carries its tier per setting; until a setting is recorded the strictest tier applies. Draft checklist: needs a clinician's check.

core_data_source: NHS England, Streamlining MDT meetings (2020), p.11 'minimum core data requirements'; aligned with the NCG Virtual Tumour Board case template (India)

post_board.record_fields_source: EUSOMA 2020 (names of all participants, evidence on decisions); Victorian Cancer MDM quality framework 2018 (report errors/changes raised, divergent recommendations and dissenting clinicians); PM-JAY HBP 2.2 s.3.9 (tumour board decision and treatment plan)

policy_basis: PM-JAY Health Benefit Package 2.2 user guidelines (NHA, 2021), section 3.9: pre-authorization is mandatory at each step of cancer care and the decision on appropriate care is to be taken by a multidisciplinary tumour board; NHS England MDT streamlining guidance (2020) pre-listing conditions. The NCG book itself asks for the board: "Multidisciplinary Tumour board" (NCG GI draft 2021: Gastric cancer, page 1); the Tumour Board Case File is that discussion, so no separate record is required for it (orchestrator, night-v3 Phase 2).
